clue.text: Daddy could make great strides as a fieldsman - ged it?

definitions.note: a description of the daddy-long-legs, which the adjective describes

blocks.note: long leg is a fielding position in cricket, and a fielder placed there
the setter tacks on the leftover letters, with a jokey 'get it?'

explanation.surface: A crane fly, nicknamed daddy, might stride across a cricket field like a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: Long leg is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side; 'ged it?' supplies the last three letters and winks at the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly is called daddy-long-legs because its limbs are very long, so it could take enormous strides.

clue.text: Direction in colour to have associate abroad

Bernard Leach was the most famous English studio potter

explanation.surface: A potter starts work by stripping the colour from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter initially' is the potter written with his first initial: B. Leach, the 20th-century St Ives potter Bernard Leach.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleaching whitens a material by chemically stripping out its dye or natural pigment.

clue.text: See 22
Villainous relative slain - clues available

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange, the dash ignored

explanation.surface: A wicked kinsman has killed someone, and detectives have plenty to go on.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Silas is the scheming guardian in Sheridan Le Fanu's Victorian mystery novel of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Le Fanu's novel is the heroine's uncle, who plots to murder her for her inheritance.

clue.text: Said to be cross about a supporter that's kept in charge of drug

explanation.surface: Someone is reportedly furious about a supporter who has been left running the drug policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plainly 'drug' at the end; the sound-play before it is Araucaria at his loosest, and no exact parse of the earlier words has been confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are synthetic hormones that build muscle tissue, banned in sport as performance-enhancing substances.

clue.text: Mushroom and some rice on cooker?

taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe: mushrooms with a little rice cooked on the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a British brand of large stove kept permanently hot, a crossword staple for cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Agaric is the botanical name for gill-bearing mushrooms such as the field mushroom and fly agaric.

clue.text: Head 16

blocks.note: first meaning: the top of the head
second meaning: the answer to 16 across, a vote at an election

explanation.walkthrough: '16' points to the answer at 16 across, GENERAL ELECTION; the word is an old term for the head as well as a word for voting.
explanation.definitionFit: Poll once meant the scalp or head, and an election is a poll because heads were counted.

clue.text: Blairite alternative to one year abroad about the spring of 1984?

blocks.note: or introduces an alternative
a well is a spring of water
Roman numeral one
an is French for year

explanation.surface: Pretends to be about Tony Blair's followers and a gap year, dated to the spring of 1984.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blairite' looks like Tony Blair's camp, but George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair, and 1984 is his novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, so anything after the manner of that writer could be called Blairite.

clue.text: Lack of protest makes one grow black

ow is a cry of complaint

explanation.surface: Seems to say that keeping quiet lets someone grow dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The O and W removed sit at either end of 'one grow', not together, which hides them well.
explanation.definitionFit: Negro is Spanish and Italian for black, and was formerly the English term for a black person, now offensive.

clue.text: Weapon with drink at side of top deck

blocks.note: a gun is a weapon
W is the abbreviation for with
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A sailor stands armed and drinking at the rail on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunwale is the upper edge of a ship's or boat's side, running along the top deck.

clue.text: Free Trade comes - Blair left party

the ten letters to work with

explanation.walkthrough: Blair is Eric Blair, Orwell, as at 9 across: his initial E is removed from 'Trade comes' and the rest rearranged, with no separate anagram signal. The Liberal Democrats are the UK's third party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberal Democrats are a British political party, so the name substitutes for party in its particular sense.

clue.text: Glasgow saint brings one back to church

indicators.note: brought back means read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A Scottish saint leads someone back to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: St Enoch is a patron of Glasgow, mother of St Mungo, remembered in St Enoch Square and station.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch, or Thenew, is venerated in Glasgow as the mother of the city's founder St Mungo.

clue.text: Churchy-sounding ointment partially baked with chips?

microchips are made of silicon

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a half-baked dish of chips with a holy-sounding ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' wants to mean fried potatoes; here it is computer chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Basilicon is an old resinous ointment whose name echoes basilica, a type of church building.

clue.text: Steer nibble around ground with dug-up flowerpots

blocks.note: taken as written
land is ground

explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of a 1950s BBC children's programme, revived in 2001, hence 'dug-up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The two puppet characters lived in flowerpots, and their show was resurrected decades later, a revival likened to digging up.

clue.text: Hen as commonly reported on page producing eggs out of team captain?

taken as written

explanation.surface: A hen laying eggs is reported in a paper, playing on a team captain left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A non-playing captain, as in Davis Cup tennis, leads a team without taking part in matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone non-playing is not taking part in the match, so is out of the team that plays.

clue.text: Going to the country? Let Greenline coach drop companion off

indicators.note: to drop a passenger is to let them get out, so those letters leave
off means gone wrong or out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A trip out of town: a Green Line coach drops off someone's travelling companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Green Line coaches ran from London out into the surrounding countryside. A prime minister 'goes to the country' by calling a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A government going to the country is asking the whole electorate to vote, which is what calling a national poll does.

clue.text: Nemesis at the ready?

blocks.note: surface reading: a goddess of retribution poised to strike
setter's reading: one who settles accounts, placed after the word 'ready' to give the name of a calculating table

explanation.surface: Retribution stands poised, ready to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Nemesis brings a day of reckoning, so she is one who reckons; 'at the ready' places her after 'ready', giving a ready reckoner, a book of precalculated tables.
explanation.definitionFit: A ready reckoner is a book of tables for quick sums, and Nemesis is one who settles scores.

clue.text: Sitting pretty, including 23 down

blocks.note: INCL is the abbreviation for including
the answer to 23 down

explanation.surface: Someone comfortably off, with everything included.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is the second word of CHANGE OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in clover is an idiom for living comfortably and prosperously, just as sitting pretty is.

Religious person eating last of porridge hasn't finished breakfast

the final letter of the word

explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a Swiss mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten as a morning cereal.

clue.text: This French student went to Salisbury

explanation.definitionFit: The earldom and later marquessate of Salisbury passed to the Cecils, so the title went to that family.

clue.text: New bowler after sixth tackle? Charlie and George upset vicar

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

an is an archaic form of and

the Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler changes at the end of each over; in rugby league possession changes after the sixth tackle.

clue.text: Always fresh work for engineers in flat
